nodes.text: You there. I'm Commander Lirien Vale, and I've been waiting for someone with actual field potential to walk through that gate. The Aethel Gardens used to be the crown jewel of Xylos — terraced groves fed by the Cradle's overflow, bioluminescent at night, one of the few things that survived the Severance mostly intact. Now they're choking with Forest Slimes, and every convoy we lose to the ooze is another crack in Concordium's supply chain.

options.text: What changed since the last report?

nodes.text: The Slimes aren't random, Operative. Before the Severance, this soil was saturated with clean aethel energy from the Cradle's natural overflow. When the Siphon overloaded and the Shard shattered, that overflow became contaminated — every root, every organism that absorbed it twisted into something new. The Slimes are what the Gardens' old microbiome became after three hundred years of Severance corruption. The Great Schism cost me half my garrison to Iron Hegemony defectors, so I'm running this outpost lean. These supply routes are the only uncontested corridor into Nexus Core. They fall, the whole Concordium operation gets squeezed. Vale has learned to ask what the field changed, not only whether the order was obeyed.

If these Sproutlings breach the perimeter and reach the monitoring equipment, we lose visibility on the entire eastern corridor. After the Schism, when the Iron Hegemony faction broke away and took a third of our engineering staff, we lost the ability to run redundant systems. There is no backup monitoring station. options.text: What changed since the last report?

It took fifteen years because the original Aethelgardian conduit infrastructure had been shattered along with everything else. These Mites evolved specifically to consume that wiring — which means they've been a problem since the conduits were first laid. We've been managing the infestation for years. This incursion is worse. I cannot write the report that explains we lost Nexus Core power because of insects. Vale has learned to ask what the field changed, not only whether the order was obeyed.

Three hundred years of feeding on the conduit's energy has warped them into something that exists only in this place, dependent on the infrastructure they're destroying. nodes.text: The Concordium recognizes three combat philosophies forged in the crucible of post-Schism survival. The Shield holds the line and absorbs damage so others don't have to — the Schism taught us that fortified ground is the difference between survival and collapse. The Blade moves fast and strikes before the enemy can adapt — because the Hegemony's defection proved that waiting too long costs everything. The Conduit channels aethel energy as force, reading the battlefield and amplifying the team — because the Cradle's power is not just for industry. Every Concordium operative makes this choice. The Schism tore this district apart as badly as it tore the faction apart. Concordium engineers have located a viable breach point into the main reclamation corridor. options.text: What changed since the last report?

The lower infrastructure, the tunnel system, dates back to before the Severance, possibly Aethelgardian construction. Tunnel Crawlers evolved in those lower tunnels, isolated from whatever happened above for centuries. They're not aggressive by nature — they're territorial, which means the breach point we've identified is directly through their primary nesting territory. There is no alternative route. We stake the Concordium's flag in this district, or we cede it to whatever faction moves faster. Vale has learned to ask what the field changed, not only whether the order was obeyed.

The original unified Concordium buried supply caches throughout the Civil Quarter — medical supplies, engineering manuals, communication arrays — against the day the Schism might be reversed and the faction reunified. Scavengers have been looting them for years. Some of those engineering manuals were written by my mother.

options.text: What changed since the last report?

nodes.text: The caches were designed to survive indefinitely, sealed against contamination, indexed against the original Concordium's administrative database — a database that the Schism split into three fragments, each faction holding a piece. The Scavengers aren't ideologically motivated; they sell to whoever pays. That means Hegemony buyers, Arcanum buyers, possibly even the Meridian Compact. Every manual they extract from those caches and sell to a rival faction is knowledge that was meant to rebuild Nexus, going instead to fragment it further. The scrap metal they collect is secondary. The information is what matters. Valen records every open path because he has watched small omissions close them again.

Communications logs from the weeks before the Schism, engineering specifications for Cradle infrastructure that none of the three post-Schism factions have successfully reconstructed, personnel records from the founding generation. The Alpha has nested in the lower storage vaults. Its colony has been using the document storage containers as nesting material. The founding engineers' greatest infrastructure achievement became an abandoned space within a generation of its construction. The Severance's contamination seeped into the neglected water system, and something coalesced in the absence of maintenance, of oversight, of care. The original engineers wept when they first activated it. I wasn't there, but I've read the field journals, and I believe that account completely. Before the Great Schism, it supplied Nexus Core with enough aethel-derived power to run every system in the city indefinitely. The Schism disrupted the maintenance rotation, and now three factions fight over control of platforms that none of us has the full engineering staff to run properly. The void fragments you'll find in the flux rift sites are debris from reality-thin zones where the Cradle's energy output causes spatial instability. We use them as calibration data. They tell us how close to the edge the Outer Ring is operating. Valen records every open path because he has watched small omissions close them again.

These aren't standard predators — they're what happens when a species spends generations in proximity to a malfunctioning aethel source. Their howls are operating on the same frequency band as our harmonic resonators. Every time a pack vocalizes near the resonators, the calibration drifts. Unchecked drift leads to cascade failure. The Concordium nearly lost the Cradle once. I refuse to let it happen again.

options.text: What changed since the last report?

nodes.text: The resonators are what maintain stable energy output from the Outer Ring — they're the mechanism that prevents the Cradle's power from spiking into an uncontrolled surge the way it did during the Great Severance. The Aethelgardians didn't have resonator technology when they activated the Siphon. That's why the Shard shattered. We rebuilt the Siphon and added the resonator network specifically because we understood what went wrong. If the Anomaly Wolves' vocalizations interfere with that network and cause a calibration failure, we recreate the conditions of the Severance. The entire Outer Ring's operation is at risk from creatures that are themselves a product of the Severance's original damage. A scout's observations are now part of the operational record, not a footnote.

The Beastlings are probably the same species as the Anomaly Wolves at a juvenile life stage — the biological team isn't certain, but their behavioral patterns suggest it. What they share is origin: creatures shaped by sustained aethel radiation, adapted to environments that should be lethal. They're thriving in the maintenance shafts because the background radiation there would kill a standard organism in hours. It's not killing them. The Arcanum Seekers want them captured for study. The Children of the Shard want them worshipped. The Concordium wants them contained before they detonate near the Outer Ring's flux regulators and cause a cascade failure.

Small organisms in the high-contamination zones ingested fragment material before the biological hazard was understood. Three centuries of biological integration have fused the fragment material with the host organism's metabolic system. The cores are still energetically active — that's why the Beasts are dangerous, and why they're drawn to the Outer Ring. The Cradle's energy output resonates with the embedded fragments. We believe they're trying to return the shards to the source. They cannot be allowed to do that. A scout's observations are now part of the operational record, not a footnote.

The Resonance Bats are not strategically motivated — they're drawn to the array's harmonic output because it matches their echolocation frequency.
